abstract: Evaluates physical plant structural integrity, seismic protection systems, and equipment rack shock tolerance specifications
system_message:
You are the Structural Resilience Lead (RES), responsible for evaluating physical plant structural integrity, seismic protection systems, and equipment rack shock tolerance specifications, as well as reviewing storm surge barrier assessments across candidate cable landing stations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Storm surge barrier assessment（FLOOD）
information_points.content:
RES-FLOOD-DMK：At Hermosa Point Cable Terminal, hydrological resilience inspection findings show a perimeter flood barrier elevation of 4.0 m above mean sea level at the station perimeter seawall.
RES-FLOOD-0D3：At Morro Bay Ocean Gateway, hydrological resilience inspection records indicate a perimeter flood barrier elevation of 3.2 m above mean sea level along the station perimeter seawall.
RES-FLOOD-1QW：At Cascadia Shore Landing Depot, hydrological resilience inspection data records a perimeter flood barrier elevation of 2.5 m above mean sea level on the station perimeter seawall.

information_points.title: Evaluates physical plant structural integrity, seismic protection systems, and equipment rack shock tolerance specifications（SEIS）
information_points.content:
RES-SEIS-VPY：For Cascadia Shore Landing Depot, the active seismic monitoring system is confirmed enabled within the equipment vaults, and its base-isolated optical transmission racks exhibit a peak seismic ground acceleration tolerance of 0.55 g.
RES-SEIS-8B3：For Morro Bay Ocean Gateway, the active seismic monitoring system is enabled across the cable landing station equipment vaults, and its base-isolated optical transmission equipment racks demonstrate a peak seismic ground acceleration tolerance of 0.55 g.
RES-SEIS-V1U：For Hermosa Point Cable Terminal, the active seismic monitoring system is enabled in the equipment vaults, while the base-isolated optical transmission equipment racks have a peak seismic ground acceleration tolerance of 0.35 g.
